question.text: A domestic corporate LP in Himalaya Arbitrage Fund has book profits of INR 20 crore for FY2025-26 and does NOT opt for Section 115BAA. Its normal-provisions tax works out to INR 2 crore. The MAT threshold under the ITA is 15% of book profits (ignore surcharge/cess for simplicity). What tax must the company pay?

answer.text: INR 3 crore (15% of book profits under MAT)
INR 2 crore (normal provisions since higher than MAT-base 0)

explanation.text: The Logic: MAT = 15% × 20 crore = INR 3 crore. Normal tax = INR 2 crore. Since MAT (3 cr) > normal tax (2 cr), the company pays MAT of INR 3 crore. The difference (1 cr) is available as MAT credit for 15 years. MAT does not apply if the company has opted for Section 115BAA/115BAB. The Trap: A picks normal provisions ignoring the MAT override. C picks the lower value, which is wrong — the rule is the HIGHER of the two. D confuses book profits with tax. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) tests MAT on Cat I/II LP side. XIX-E tests it for Cat III LPs who receive fund-distributed income that they must still aggregate for book-profit MAT computation. XXI-B also tests MAT for corporate PMS clients. Manager's Pro-Tip: When onboarding a domestic corporate LP at Himalaya, warn them that NAV-embedded, fund-taxed income still enters THEIR book profits for MAT computation — even though the fund has already paid MMR. This creates a cash-tax spike even when fund distributions are nil.
